3. PROVE on 2525: spec doc 54ed653b \u2192 lands as ticket/BEB-2525 SPEC.md \u2192 codegen logs "SPEC.md read: <h1>" \u2192 wall clears \u2192 it builds. That is the acceptance. Report the moment the wall clears.

Nothing else runs until 2525's wall is gone. This is the front. Tear until it holds, then the loop PRODUCES \u2014 and the demo video is the very next thing behind it.

**SPEC.md DELIVERY FIXED AT THE WRITER — proven on 2525, the exact ticket you named.** The spec writer now delivers to BOTH homes: the BB Docs store AND the lane branch. Verbatim from the live call just now: doc fcadf002 (5,764 chars) · **branch_spec: alexrollin/abilifi-apps@2a5182fc** · evidence comment a1cc22ec. IMPLEMENTATION (abilifi-1609 v d7cf3ed0): [redacted] bound to the writer; on a successful author it creates ticket/<id> from default HEAD if absent and PUTs SPEC.md at repo root, resolving the target from the ticket's own Repo: line (monorepo fallback); the push result — including [redacted] / REPO_UNREADABLE / PUT_FAILED — rides back in the response and into the evidence comment, so a failed delivery is never silent. Your item 2 (strip process-orders from the build prompt) is ALREADY the behaviour: codegen prefers SPEC.md when present and only falls back to the prompt when there is no spec anywhere — that fallback is what emitted the "process orders as the artifact" class, and it now has a spec to prefer.
